public_rationale: Research documents substantial circulation of AI images and a small contemporaneous feed audit. Neither establishes that AI slop dominated ordinary Facebook feeds. The available evidence also does not establish that its share was small, so contradiction would be unwarranted.
limitations: The strongest exposure study sampled pages already known to publish AI images.
The contemporaneous pilot used only four artificial accounts.
The result depends partly on whether dominating means typical feed prevalence or prominence in some users' experiences.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Bizarre AI-generated slop is dominating Facebook feeds.

statement.excerpt: bizarre AI slop is dominating feeds with Mark Zuckerberg promising that there’s more to come

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that low-quality AI-generated material occupied a prevailing share of ordinary Facebook feed exposure, beyond isolated viral posts.
The current-state observation is assessed over December 1–16, 2024, the elapsed portion of the publication month. The speaker supplies no reporting interval.
The reference to Zuckerberg is background to the supplied proposition, not a separate forecast being graded.
criteria.support_condition: Representative contemporaneous feed measurements show that low-quality AI-generated content occupied a prevailing share of what ordinary Facebook users saw.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporaneous measurements show that such content occupied only a small share of ordinary Facebook feed exposure.

evidence.excerpt: These images collectively received hundreds of millions of exposures.
evidence.explanation: The study examined 125 pages already selected for posting AI images. Its substantial exposure totals do not measure the proportion of ordinary feeds occupied by AI content, and its observations precede the target period.

evidence.locator: Methods at the edge of access
evidence.explanation: The pilot collected images from four newly created accounts between November 27 and December 5, 2024. It describes image themes but supplies neither a representative user sample nor the share of all feed impressions attributable to AI slop.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative audit of December 2024 Facebook feeds measuring low-quality AI-generated impressions against all feed impressions.
